basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the procedural container of a dispute in one forum, not the dispute, claim or underlying event.
Keeps filings, evidence and judgments as child records with their own identity.
Separates allegations, findings, orders and enforceable judgments as distinct states.
Links appeals, recognition and enforcement as separate cases rather than extending this one.

may: Docket filings and compute procedural deadlines from forum rules for checking.
Schedule hearings and send service notices on instruction of the registry.
Prepare a case chronology or index of filings for the tribunal.
Check filings for format and completeness against forum rules.
mustNot: Issue or draft as final any order, finding, judgment or award.
Disclose sealed, confidential or anonymised material to unauthorised parties.
Treat an allegation or admitted exhibit as an established fact.
Change the docket record after the fact without a correction entry.
Communicate with one party about the merits outside the forum procedure.
requiresHuman: Any adjudicative or adverse procedural decision.
Unsealing, anonymisation choices and publication of case material.
Declaring finality, closure or reopening of a case.

considerations: Due process, equality of arms and the right to be heard must not be weakened by automation.
Case records expose parties, witnesses and minors to stigma; disclosure must follow anonymisation rules.
Missed deadlines computed wrongly can cost a party its claim or defence.
affectedParties: Witnesses, victims and minors named in the case

items: A case has a forum, a case number, parties in procedural roles and a docket of dated events.
It is confused with the underlying dispute, a single filing, a judgment or an enforcement case.
Wrong deadline computation leading to default or forfeiture.
Leak of sealed evidence or witness identity.
Misattribution of a filing to the wrong case or party.
Akoma Ntoso for judgments and orders.
e-CODEX for cross-border judicial exchange in the EU.
